stem: You are reviewing a hand-written OpenQASM 3 program and want to keep only declarations the language actually defines. Exactly one of the following lines is a legal classical declaration in OpenQASM 3. Which one?

explanation.correct: `angle` is one of OpenQASM 3's four *special* classical types — the ones with no C equivalent — alongside `bit`, `duration` and `stretch`; the standard ones are `bool`, `int`, `uint`, `float` and `complex`. Sized types carry their width in a designator, so `angle[16] phi;` declares a 16-bit fixed-point angle, interpreted modulo 2π and promoted like an unsigned integer when mixed with other angles. Everything else in the language's classical inventory follows the same `type[size] name;` shape: `int[32] n;`, `uint[8] k;`, `float[64] x;`, `bit[4] c;`.

distractors.A: There is no character type in OpenQASM 3: the language has no text data at all, so nothing like `char` or a character literal exists.
distractors.B: Right type, wrong designator. A complex number is declared `complex[float[size]] amp;` — the designator names the floating-point type used for the two components — and a bare `complex` is shorthand for `complex[float]`. A raw bit width in the brackets is not accepted.
distractors.C: `real` is the Verilog/VHDL spelling. OpenQASM 3 calls its floating-point type `float`, declared as `float[64] theta;`.
distractors.E: There is no string type. The only place quoted text appears is the `include "stdgates.inc";` directive and bit-literal initializers such as `bit[8] b = "00001111";`.
distractors.F: The unsigned integer type is spelled `uint`, so this would be `uint[8] shots;`. C's `unsigned` modifier is not part of the grammar.

provenance.notes: official-alignment gap task 8.1: the OpenQASM 3 type system was covered only through Qiskit's feature table. Authored from the openqasm.com 3.0 types page (type inventory + declaration grammar), with an option set of its own — no execution is possible here because `qiskit-qasm3-import` is NOT installed in the pinned env (re-checked 2026-07-26: ModuleNotFoundError), and Qiskit's importer is in any case narrower than the language, so a loads()-based proof would refute legal OpenQASM.
